question: Two wires of the same material have equal lengths but their cross-sectional areas are in the ratio 1 : 4. The ratio of their resistances will be:
solution_text:
The correct answer is 4 : 1.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Resistance of a wire is given by R = ρL/A, where ρ is resistivity, L is length and A is the cross-sectional area.

 

• Since both wires are of the same material (same ρ) and have equal length (same L), resistance is inversely proportional to the area (R ∝ 1/A). (प्रतिरोध — R = ρL/A)

 

• Given A1 : A2 = 1 : 4, so R1 : R2 = (1/A1) : (1/A2) = 4 : 1.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option B.

 

Additional Information

 

• Resistivity (ρ) is a property of the material and does not change with the shape or size of the wire; it changes with temperature.

 

• Doubling the length of a wire doubles its resistance; doubling its cross-sectional area halves its resistance.

 

NOTE

 

• 1 : 1 (Option A): True only if the areas were also equal, which is not the case here.

 

• 1 : 4 (Option C): The inverse of the correct ratio — a common calculation slip.

 

• 1 : 2 (Option D): Does not follow from R ∝ 1/A for the given area ratio.

question: An atom has 11 protons, 11 electrons and 12 neutrons. What is the mass number of that atom?
solution_text:
The correct answer is 23.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The mass number (A) of an atom is the total number of protons + neutrons in its nucleus; electrons are not counted as they have negligible mass. (द्रव्यमान संख्या — प्रोटॉन + न्यूट्रॉन)

 

• Here, protons = 11 and neutrons = 12, so mass number = 11 + 12 = 23.

 

• The number of protons alone (11) gives the atomic number, which identifies the element as sodium (Na).

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option C.

 

Additional Information

 

• Since protons = electrons = 11, the atom is electrically neutral.

 

• Isotopes of an element have the same atomic number but different mass numbers (different neutron counts).

 

NOTE

 

• 24 (Option A): Would be the mass number only if neutrons were 13.

 

• 11 (Option B): This is the atomic number (number of protons), not the mass number.

 

• 12 (Option D): This is just the number of neutrons, not the mass number.

question: Which of the following statements is INCORRECT about uniform motion?
option_2: The speed varies continuously with time
option_4: The body covers equal distances in equal intervals of time
solution_text:
The correct answer is The speed varies continuously with time.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• In uniform motion, a body covers equal distances in equal intervals of time, so its speed (and velocity, if direction is also fixed) stays constant. (एकसमान गति — स्थिर चाल)

 

• Since velocity does not change, the rate of change of velocity, i.e. acceleration, is zero.

 

• The statement that speed varies continuously describes non-uniform (accelerated) motion, not uniform motion, so it is the incorrect statement here.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option B.

 

Additional Information

 

• A body moving with uniform velocity has zero acceleration; a body moving with uniform acceleration has a constant rate of change of velocity (e.g., a freely falling body).

 

• On a distance-time graph, uniform motion is represented by a straight line, while non-uniform motion gives a curved line.

 

NOTE

 

• The velocity remains unchanged (Option A): A true statement about uniform motion.

 

• The acceleration is zero (Option C): A true statement, since velocity is constant.

 

• The body covers equal distances in equal intervals of time (Option D): This is the very definition of uniform motion, hence true.

question: During the process of electrolytic refining of metals, on passing the current through the electrolyte, the impure metal from the ______ dissolves into the electrolyte.
solution_text:
The correct answer is anode.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• In electrolytic refining, the impure metal is made the anode and a thin strip of the pure metal is made the cathode, both dipped in a solution (electrolyte) of the metal's salt. (विद्युत-अपघटनी शोधन — अशुद्ध धातु ऐनोड)

 

• On passing current, the impure metal at the anode dissolves into the electrolyte as metal ions, and an equivalent amount of pure metal deposits at the cathode.

 

• The insoluble impurities (like other metals) settle down at the bottom of the anode as anode mud (or anode sludge), which often contains valuable metals like silver and gold.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option D.

 

Additional Information

 

• This method is commonly used to refine copper, silver, gold, zinc, tin and nickel.

 

• For copper refining, the electrolyte used is acidified copper sulphate solution.

 

NOTE

 

• Salt bridge (Option A): Used in electrochemical (galvanic) cells to complete the circuit and maintain electrical neutrality; not part of electrolytic refining.

 

• Both anode and cathode (Option B): Only the anode dissolves; the cathode gains, not loses, metal.

 

• Cathode (Option C): This is where pure metal gets deposited, not dissolved.

question: Which gas is mainly responsible for the greenhouse effect and is released when fossil fuels are burned?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Carbon dioxide.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Carbon dioxide (CO2) is the greenhouse gas most responsible for the greenhouse effect and global warming caused by human activity, and is released in large quantities when fossil fuels (coal, petroleum, natural gas) are burned. (कार्बन डाइऑक्साइड — ग्रीनहाउस प्रभाव)

 

• Greenhouse gases trap infrared (heat) radiation reflected from the Earth's surface, keeping the atmosphere warmer than it would otherwise be — the natural greenhouse effect is essential for life, but excess CO2 causes enhanced global warming.

 

• Other important greenhouse gases include methane, nitrous oxide, water vapour and chlorofluorocarbons (CFCs), though CO2 contributes the largest share due to the sheer scale of fossil-fuel combustion.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option C.

 

Additional Information

 

• The Kyoto Protocol (1997) and the Paris Agreement (2015) are major international treaties aimed at reducing greenhouse gas emissions.

 

• Current atmospheric CO2 concentration is over 420 ppm, up from about 280 ppm in the pre-industrial era.

 

NOTE

 

• Oxygen (Option A) and Nitrogen (Option B): Together make up about 99% of the atmosphere but are not greenhouse gases.

 

• Hydrogen (Option D): Not a significant atmospheric greenhouse gas.

question: Which of the following statements is NOT correct?
option_1: In a prism, the incident ray and emergent ray are always parallel.
option_2: In a prism, dispersion can occur if white light is used.
option_3: In a prism, the emergent ray bends towards the base of the prism when the incident ray is coming from the base side.
option_4: The angle of deviation is the angle between the incident ray and emergent ray.
solution_text:
The correct answer is In a prism, the incident ray and emergent ray are always parallel.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• A prism always bends light towards its base (refracts it), so the emergent ray is generally not parallel to the incident ray — the angle between them is called the angle of deviation. (प्रिज्म — विचलन कोण)

 

• If white light passes through a prism, its different colour components (each with a different refractive index/wavelength) bend by different amounts, causing dispersion — the splitting of white light into the VIBGYOR spectrum.

 

• Since a prism has two non-parallel refracting surfaces, unlike a rectangular glass slab, there is no situation in which the incident and emergent rays become parallel, making this the incorrect statement.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option A.

 

Additional Information

 

• In a rectangular glass slab, by contrast, the emergent ray IS parallel to the incident ray (only laterally displaced), because the two refracting surfaces are parallel to each other.

 

• Violet light deviates the most and red light the least when passing through a prism, since violet has the shortest wavelength and highest refractive index in glass.

 

NOTE

 

• Dispersion with white light (Option B): A correct statement — this is exactly how a prism produces a spectrum.

 

• Emergent ray bending towards the base (Option C): Correct — light always bends towards the base of the prism on refraction.

 

• Angle of deviation (Option D): Correctly defines the angle of deviation.

question: Which of the following ensures genetic variation in sexually reproducing animals?
option_2: Offspring receive genes from both parents
solution_text:
The correct answer is Offspring receive genes from both parents.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• In sexual reproduction, the offspring receives half of its genes from the male parent and half from the female parent, through the fusion of sperm and egg. This mixing of two different sets of genes is the main source of genetic variation. (लैंगिक जनन — आनुवंशिक विविधता)

 

• Gametes are formed by meiosis (not mitosis), a reductive cell division that also introduces variation through crossing over and independent assortment of chromosomes.

 

• Genetic variation is important for a species because it increases the chances that at least some individuals will survive changing environmental conditions, forming the raw material for natural selection.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option B.

 

Additional Information

 

• Asexual reproduction (budding, binary fission, vegetative propagation) produces offspring genetically identical to the single parent (clones), with variation arising only from occasional mutation.

 

• DNA copying is never 100% exact; small errors during replication are another natural source of variation.

 

NOTE

 

• Gametes are formed by mitosis (Option A): Incorrect — gametes are formed by meiosis, which halves the chromosome number.

 

• Only one parent is involved (Option C): This describes asexual reproduction, which produces genetically identical offspring, not variation.

 

• Fertilisation occurs inside the body (Option D): This describes internal fertilisation, a mode of reproduction, but is not itself the cause of genetic variation.

question: Which of the following observations confirms that a solution is acidic?
option_1: Methyl orange: red, Phenolphthalein: colourless, Litmus: red
option_2: Methyl orange: yellow, Phenolphthalein: pink, Litmus: blue
option_3: Methyl orange: red, Phenolphthalein: pink, Litmus: red
option_4: Methyl orange: yellow, Phenolphthalein: colourless, Litmus: blue
solution_text:
The correct answer is Methyl orange: red, Phenolphthalein: colourless, Litmus: red.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Acid-base indicators change colour depending on whether a solution is acidic, neutral or basic. (सूचक — अम्ल में रंग परिवर्तन)

 

• In an acidic solution: methyl orange turns red, phenolphthalein remains colourless, and blue litmus turns red (litmus stays/becomes red).

 

• In a basic solution the pattern reverses: methyl orange turns yellow, phenolphthalein turns pink, and red litmus turns blue.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option A.

 

Additional Information

 

• Litmus is a natural indicator extracted from lichens; it turns red in acid and blue in base, and is purple in neutral solution.

 

• Other natural indicators include turmeric (turns reddish-brown in base) and red cabbage extract.

 

NOTE

 

• Methyl orange yellow, Phenolphthalein pink, Litmus blue (Option B): This is the correct pattern for a basic solution, not acidic.

 

• Methyl orange red, Phenolphthalein pink, Litmus red (Option C): An inconsistent mix — phenolphthalein does not turn pink in an acidic solution.

 

• Methyl orange yellow, Phenolphthalein colourless, Litmus blue (Option D): An inconsistent mix of basic (yellow, blue litmus) and acidic/neutral (colourless) indications; does not represent a genuinely acidic solution.

question: Based on function, which of the following combinations represent all types of animal tissues found in humans?
option_1: Epithelial tissue, Muscular tissue and Glandular tissue
option_2: Epithelial tissue, Connective tissue and Reproductive tissue
option_3: Epithelial tissue, Connective tissue and Skeletal tissue
option_4: Epithelial tissue, Connective tissue, Muscular tissue and Nervous tissue
solution_text:
The correct answer is Epithelial tissue, Connective tissue, Muscular tissue and Nervous tissue.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Animal tissues are classified, on the basis of the function they perform, into four basic types: Epithelial, Connective, Muscular and Nervous tissue. (चार प्रकार के जंतु ऊतक)

 

• Epithelial tissue covers and lines body surfaces and cavities (skin, gut lining) and provides protection.

 

• Connective tissue binds and supports other tissues (bone, cartilage, blood, adipose tissue); muscular tissue enables movement (skeletal, smooth, cardiac muscle); nervous tissue carries and processes electrical impulses (neurons).

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option D.

 

Additional Information

 

• Blood is classified as a fluid connective tissue because its matrix (plasma) is liquid.

 

• Skeletal tissue (bone and cartilage) is a type of connective tissue, not a separate fifth category.

 

NOTE

 

• Epithelial, Muscular and Glandular (Option A): Glandular tissue is a specialised form of epithelial tissue, not a separate fourth category, and this list omits connective and nervous tissue.

 

• Epithelial, Connective and Reproductive (Option B): 'Reproductive tissue' is not one of the four basic tissue types; muscular and nervous tissue are missing.

 

• Epithelial, Connective and Skeletal (Option C): Skeletal tissue is a sub-type of connective tissue, not an independent fourth type; muscular and nervous tissue are missing.

question: Which plastids contain pigments that give plants their yellow, orange or red colours?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Chromoplasts.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Chromoplasts are coloured plastids that contain pigments such as carotenoids and xanthophylls, giving fruits, flowers and some roots their yellow, orange or red colours (e.g. tomato, carrot, chilli). (वर्णीलवक — पीला/नारंगी/लाल रंग)

 

• Plastids are a family of organelles found in plant cells, classified by their pigment content into three main types: chloroplasts (green), chromoplasts (yellow/orange/red) and leucoplasts (colourless).

 

• Chromoplasts often develop from chloroplasts as a fruit ripens, which is why unripe fruits (green, due to chlorophyll) turn red, orange or yellow as they mature.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option D.

 

Additional Information

 

• Leucoplasts are colourless plastids used for storage; they include amyloplasts (starch), elaioplasts (oils/fats) and aleuroplasts (proteins).

 

• Chloroplasts contain chlorophyll and are the site of photosynthesis.

 

NOTE

 

• Amyloplasts (Option A): A colourless leucoplast that stores starch, found in tubers like potato.

 

• Leucoplasts (Option B): The general colourless, storage-type plastid, not the pigmented ones.

 

• Chloroplasts (Option C): Contain green chlorophyll and carry out photosynthesis, not the source of yellow/orange/red colours.

question: What is the main function of the vas deferens in the male reproductive system?
option_1: Transporting sperm from the epididymis to the urethra
solution_text:
The correct answer is Transporting sperm from the epididymis to the urethra.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The vas deferens (sperm duct) is a long, muscular tube whose main function is to carry mature sperm from the epididymis to the urethra during ejaculation, using peristaltic contractions. (शुक्रवाहिका — शुक्राणु परिवहन)

 

• Sperm mature and are stored in the epididymis, a coiled tube lying on top of the testis, before being transported onward.

 

• Along the way, secretions from the seminal vesicles and prostate gland join the sperm to form semen, which then passes through the urethra and out of the body.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option A.

 

Additional Information

 

• Sperm production (spermatogenesis) occurs in the seminiferous tubules of the testes, not the vas deferens.

 

• A vasectomy, a method of male sterilisation, involves cutting and sealing the vas deferens to block sperm transport.

 

NOTE

 

• Sperm production (Option B): This is the function of the seminiferous tubules within the testes.

 

• Regulating body temperature (Option C): This is the role of the scrotum, which keeps the testes slightly cooler than body temperature.

 

• Seminal fluid secretion (Option D): This is performed by the seminal vesicles and prostate gland, not the vas deferens itself.

question: What is the role of lysosomes in a cell?
solution_text:
The correct answer is To digest foreign material.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Lysosomes are membrane-bound organelles filled with powerful digestive (hydrolytic) enzymes that break down worn-out cell organelles, foreign material and food particles taken in by the cell. (लाइसोसोम — आत्मघाती थैली)

 

• They are often called the 'suicide bags' of the cell, because if the cell is damaged or dies, lysosomes can rupture and digest the cell's own contents.

 

• Lysosomes are especially abundant in white blood cells (phagocytes), where they digest bacteria and other pathogens engulfed by the cell.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option A.

 

Additional Information

 

• Lysosomes are formed by the Golgi apparatus and were discovered by Christian de Duve.

 

• They typically contain enzymes that work best at acidic pH, matching the acidic interior of the lysosome.

 

NOTE

 

• To transport products (Option B): This is a role of the Golgi apparatus and endoplasmic reticulum, not lysosomes.

 

• To produce ATP (Option C): This is the function of the mitochondria, the 'powerhouse of the cell'.

 

• To store proteins (Option D): Proteins are largely processed and packaged by the Golgi apparatus, not stored by lysosomes.

question: Which of the following statements is true about magnetic field lines?
option_1: Field lines inside a magnet move from north to south.
option_2: Magnetic field is weaker where lines are close.
option_4: Field lines outside a magnet move from north to south.
solution_text:
The correct answer is Field lines outside a magnet move from north to south.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Magnetic field lines are conventionally drawn to emerge from the north pole and re-enter at the south pole outside the magnet, forming continuous closed loops. (चुंबकीय क्षेत्र रेखाएँ — N से S बाहर)

 

• Inside the magnet, the field lines travel in the opposite direction, from the south pole to the north pole, so as to form closed loops overall.

 

• Field lines are always denser where the field is stronger (e.g. near the poles), not weaker — so 'weaker where lines are close' is the opposite of the truth.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option D.

 

Additional Information

 

• Magnetic field lines never intersect each other — if they did, it would mean the field has two directions at that point, which is impossible.

 

• The tangent drawn to a field line at any point gives the direction of the magnetic field at that point.

 

NOTE

 

• Field lines inside a magnet move from north to south (Option A): Incorrect — inside the magnet, they go from south to north.

 

• Magnetic field is weaker where lines are close (Option B): Incorrect — closely spaced lines indicate a stronger field.

 

• Field lines intersect at poles (Option C): Incorrect — field lines never intersect anywhere, including at the poles.

question: A machine does 'W' joule work in time 't' seconds. The power 'P' watt of the machine is given correctly by which of the following relations?
solution_text:
The correct answer is P = W/t.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Power is defined as the rate of doing work, i.e., work done per unit time: P = W/t. (शक्ति — कार्य/समय)

 

• Its SI unit is the watt (W), where 1 watt = 1 joule/second — the power of a machine that does 1 joule of work in 1 second.

 

• Power is a scalar quantity, and larger values of P mean work is being done faster for the same amount of work W.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option C.

 

Additional Information

 

• Another common commercial unit of power is the horsepower (1 hp ≈ 746 W).

 

• The unit of electrical energy commonly used is the kilowatt-hour (kWh) — the energy consumed by a 1000 W appliance running for 1 hour.

 

NOTE

 

• P = W²/t (Option A) and P = W²t (Option B): Dimensionally and physically incorrect — power does not involve the square of work.

 

• P = W × t (Option D): This would give a quantity with units of joule-seconds, not watts; it is not the formula for power.

question: According to Bohr's Model of atom, electrons revolve around the nucleus in __________.
solution_text:
The correct answer is discrete orbits.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Niels Bohr's model of the atom (1913) proposed that electrons revolve around the nucleus only in certain fixed, discrete circular orbits (energy levels or shells), each having a definite energy. (बोर मॉडल — असतत कक्षाएँ)

 

• Electrons do not radiate energy while moving in these permitted orbits; they gain or lose energy only when they jump from one orbit to another, absorbing or emitting a photon of a specific energy.

 

• These orbits are labelled by the principal quantum number n = 1, 2, 3, ... (also called K, L, M, N shells), and each orbit can hold a maximum of 2n² electrons.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option A.

 

Additional Information

 

• Bohr's model successfully explained the hydrogen spectrum but could not fully explain the spectra of multi-electron atoms — this was later refined by quantum mechanics.

 

• Bohr's model was an improvement on Rutherford's nuclear model, which could not explain why orbiting electrons don't spiral into the nucleus.

 

NOTE

 

• Elliptical path (Option B): This modification was proposed later by Sommerfeld, not in Bohr's original model.

 

• Random path (Option C): Contradicts Bohr's postulate of fixed, well-defined orbits.

 

• Straight lines (Option D): Electrons in Bohr's model move in closed circular orbits, not straight lines.

question: Which of the following is NOT considered an organic compound?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Sodium carbonate (Na2CO3).

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Sodium carbonate (Na2CO3) is classified as an inorganic compound; although it contains carbon, simple carbonates, oxides, cyanides and a few other carbon compounds are traditionally treated as exceptions and grouped with inorganic chemistry. (कार्बोनेट — अकार्बनिक यौगिक का अपवाद)

 

• Organic compounds are, by definition, compounds of carbon typically containing carbon-hydrogen bonds and are associated with living organisms — such as acetic acid, methane and ethanol, all of which are carbon-hydrogen based compounds.

 

• Methane (CH4) is the simplest hydrocarbon, ethanol (C2H5OH) is an alcohol, and acetic acid (CH3COOH) is a carboxylic acid — all classic organic compounds.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option D.

 

Additional Information

 

• Other common exceptions treated as inorganic despite containing carbon: carbon dioxide (CO2), carbon monoxide (CO), and metal cyanides/carbides.

 

• Organic chemistry is sometimes called the 'chemistry of carbon compounds' because carbon's ability to form long chains and rings (catenation) gives rise to millions of organic compounds.

 

NOTE

 

• Acetic acid (Option A): The organic acid present in vinegar; a carboxylic acid.

 

• Methane (Option B): The simplest hydrocarbon and the main component of natural gas/biogas.

 

• Ethanol (Option C): A common alcohol, an organic compound used as a solvent and biofuel.

question: An object is thrown straight up and reaches a maximum height of 20 m. If we take g = 10 m/sec², what was the initial speed of the object when it was thrown?
solution_text:
The correct answer is 20 m/sec.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• For an object thrown straight up, at maximum height the final velocity becomes zero; the relevant equation of motion is v² = u² − 2gh. (ऊर्ध्वाधर प्रक्षेप्य गति)

 

• Substituting v = 0, g = 10 m/s², h = 20 m: 0 = u² − 2(10)(20) ⇒ u² = 400 ⇒ u = 20 m/s.

 

• This means the object must have been thrown upward with an initial speed of 20 m/s to just reach a height of 20 m before momentarily stopping and falling back.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option D.

 

Additional Information

 

• The time taken to reach maximum height is given by t = u/g = 20/10 = 2 seconds, and the object takes an equal time to fall back, so total time of flight = 4 seconds (ignoring air resistance).

 

• At maximum height, the object's velocity is zero but its acceleration is still g (downward), not zero.

 

NOTE

 

• 40 m/sec (Option A): Would give a maximum height of u²/2g = 1600/20 = 80 m, not 20 m.

 

• 30 m/sec (Option B): Would give a maximum height of 900/20 = 45 m, not 20 m.

 

• 10 m/sec (Option C): Would give a maximum height of 100/20 = 5 m, not 20 m.

question: What is the formula of formic acid?
solution_text:
The correct answer is HCOOH.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Formic acid (methanoic acid) has the chemical formula HCOOH, the simplest carboxylic acid. (फॉर्मिक अम्ल — चींटी के डंक में)

 

• It is naturally found in the stings and bites of ants and bees and in the hairs of nettle leaves, and is responsible for the burning/itching sensation they cause.

 

• It contains one carboxyl group (-COOH) attached to a hydrogen atom, making it the smallest member of the carboxylic acid family.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option B.

 

Additional Information

 

• C2H4O2 (Option A) is the molecular formula of acetic acid written differently (CH3COOH has molecular formula C2H4O2), which can cause confusion, but the standard structural formula for acetic acid is CH3COOH, not formic acid.

 

• Formic acid is used in textile dyeing, leather tanning and as a preservative/antibacterial agent in livestock feed.

 

NOTE

 

• C2H4O2 (Option A): This is the molecular formula of acetic acid (CH3COOH), not formic acid.

 

• C2H5OH (Option C): This is the formula of ethanol, an alcohol, not an acid.

 

• C2H6O (Option D): This is another way of writing ethanol's molecular formula, not formic acid.

question: Which of the following carbon compounds burns with a blue, non-sooty flame under normal conditions?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Ethanol.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Ethanol, like other saturated compounds with a high oxygen-to-carbon ratio, undergoes fairly complete combustion in air, producing a clean, blue, non-sooty flame. (इथेनॉल — नीली, धुआँरहित लौ)

 

• A blue flame indicates that the fuel is burning with sufficient oxygen supply, giving complete combustion to CO2 and H2O without leaving unburnt carbon particles (soot).

 

• Fuels rich in carbon relative to hydrogen (like diesel, kerosene and charcoal) tend to burn with a yellow, sooty flame due to incomplete combustion and glowing unburnt carbon particles.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option B.

 

Additional Information

 

• LPG and CNG also typically burn with a clean blue flame when supplied with adequate air, which is why they are considered cleaner fuels.

 

• Sooty (yellow) flames deposit carbon (soot) on surfaces and indicate incomplete combustion, releasing less heat per unit fuel.

 

NOTE

 

• Diesel (Option A): A heavier hydrocarbon that typically burns with a yellow, sooty flame in ordinary combustion.

 

• Kerosene (Option C): Also usually burns with a yellow, somewhat sooty flame in an open wick lamp.

 

• Charcoal (Option D): Solid carbon; it glows and burns with a yellow-orange flame, producing soot/ash.

question: A net horizontal force of 20 N acts on a 4 kg block initially at rest for 5 s. What is the block's final speed?
solution_text:
The correct answer is 25 m/s.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• By Newton's second law, F = ma, so acceleration a = F/m = 20/4 = 5 m/s². (न्यूटन का द्वितीय नियम)

 

• Using v = u + at, with u = 0 (starts at rest), a = 5 m/s², t = 5 s: v = 0 + 5 × 5 = 25 m/s.

 

• Since the block starts from rest and the force acts for the full 5 seconds with constant acceleration, this gives the final speed directly.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option D.

 

Additional Information

 

• The distance covered in this time can also be found: s = ut + ½at² = 0 + ½(5)(25) = 62.5 m.

 

• Newton's second law in its more general form is F = dp/dt, the rate of change of momentum.

 

NOTE

 

• 30 m/s, 50 m/s, 20 m/s (Options A, B, C): Do not match v = u + at for a = 5 m/s² and t = 5 s; each represents a common arithmetic slip (e.g. mixing up F and a, or the time).

question: Which of the following is a key goal of conserving forests and biodiversity?
option_1: To allow more industrial use of forests
solution_text:
The correct answer is To preserve inherited biodiversity.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The central goal of forest and biodiversity conservation is to preserve the variety of life (biodiversity) inherited from nature for future generations, maintaining ecological balance, gene pools and ecosystem services. (जैव विविधता संरक्षण)

 

• Conservation aims to prevent the loss of species, habitats and genetic diversity caused by deforestation, pollution, over-exploitation and climate change.

 

• Protecting biodiversity also safeguards essential ecosystem services such as clean air and water, soil fertility, pollination and climate regulation, on which human life ultimately depends.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option D.

 

Additional Information

 

• India is one of the world's 17 megadiverse countries and has four biodiversity hotspots: the Himalayas, the Western Ghats, the Indo-Burma region and Sundaland (Nicobar Islands).

 

• Sustainable use (using resources without depleting them for future generations) is a core principle alongside conservation.

 

NOTE

 

• To allow more industrial use of forests (Option A): Contrary to conservation goals, which aim to limit exploitative use.

 

• To promote tourism (Option B): Ecotourism can be a secondary benefit, but it is not the core purpose of conservation.

 

• To expand national parks (Option C): Creating protected areas is one tool used for conservation, but it is a means, not the ultimate goal itself.

question: An object is placed 30 cm in front of a concave mirror of focal length 15 cm. What will be the image distance v?
solution_text:
The correct answer is −30 cm.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Using the Cartesian sign convention, distances measured against the incident light (towards the object side) are negative, so for a concave mirror u = −30 cm and f = −15 cm. (दर्पण सूत्र — 1/v + 1/u = 1/f)

 

• The mirror formula is 1/v + 1/u = 1/f. Substituting: 1/v = 1/f − 1/u = 1/(−15) − 1/(−30) = −1/15 + 1/30 = −2/30 + 1/30 = −1/30.

 

• So v = −30 cm, meaning the image forms 30 cm in front of the mirror — on the same side as the object.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option A.

 

Additional Information

 

• Since the object here is at twice the focal length (u = 2f), the image also forms at 2f (v = −30 cm) — this special case gives a real, inverted, same-size image, a standard fact for concave mirrors.

 

• For a concave mirror, when the object is placed beyond the centre of curvature (C), a real, inverted, diminished image forms between F and C.

 

NOTE

 

• −15 cm (Option B): Equals the focal length, not the actual image distance for u = −30 cm.

 

• +30 cm and +15 cm (Options C and D): Positive signs would indicate a virtual image behind the mirror, which is incorrect here since the object lies beyond the focus, producing a real image in front of the mirror.

question: If tall (T) is dominant over short (t), and round seeds (R) are dominant over wrinkled (r), identify the genotype of a plant that shows short height and round seeds.
solution_text:
The correct answer is ttRR.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• A short plant must be homozygous recessive for height (tt), because 'short' is the recessive trait — if even one dominant T allele were present, the plant would be tall. (मेंडल के आनुवंशिकी नियम — प्रभावी/अप्रभावी लक्षण)

 

• A round-seeded plant, since round (R) is dominant, could genotypically be either RR (homozygous) or Rr (heterozygous) — round seeds alone don't tell us which.

 

• Among the given options, only ttRR correctly shows the recessive homozygous genotype for the recessive short trait combined with a round-seed genotype.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option D.

 

Additional Information

 

• This scenario is modelled on Gregor Mendel's classic pea plant experiments, which established the laws of dominance, segregation and independent assortment.

 

• A test cross (crossing with a homozygous recessive) is the standard method used to determine whether a dominant-trait individual is homozygous or heterozygous.

 

NOTE

 

• TtRr (Option A): Heterozygous for height would produce a tall plant (T dominant), not short.

 

• TtRR (Option B): Also heterozygous for height, so the plant would be tall, not short.

 

• Ttrr (Option C): Heterozygous Tt would still give a tall plant, and rr would give wrinkled (not round) seeds — matches neither trait required.

question: Which of the following correctly defines the amplitude of a wave?
option_1: The distance between two consecutive crests
option_2: The maximum displacement of the particle from its mean position
option_3: The speed with which the wave travels
option_4: The number of vibrations per second
solution_text:
The correct answer is The maximum displacement of the particle from its mean position.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The amplitude of a wave is defined as the maximum displacement of a vibrating particle of the medium from its mean (equilibrium/rest) position. (आयाम — माध्य स्थिति से अधिकतम विस्थापन)

 

• Amplitude determines the loudness of a sound wave (in the case of sound) or the intensity/energy carried by the wave in general — larger amplitude means more energy.

 

• It is measured in units of length (e.g. metres) for a mechanical wave, since it represents a displacement.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option B.

 

Additional Information

 

• The distance between two consecutive crests (or troughs) is called the wavelength (λ).

 

• The number of vibrations per second is called the frequency (f), measured in hertz (Hz), and relates to speed by v = fλ.

 

NOTE

 

• Distance between two consecutive crests (Option A): This defines wavelength, not amplitude.

 

• Speed with which the wave travels (Option C): This is the wave speed/velocity, a separate wave property.

 

• Number of vibrations per second (Option D): This defines frequency, not amplitude.

question: Which property of isobars is always different?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Atomic number.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Isobars are atoms of different elements that happen to have the same mass number but a different number of protons (atomic number) and, correspondingly, a different number of neutrons. (समभारिक — समान द्रव्यमान संख्या, भिन्न परमाणु क्रमांक)

 

• Since isobars belong to different elements by definition, their atomic number (number of protons) is always different — this is, in fact, the defining distinguishing feature between them.

 

• Classic examples of isobars: Argon-40, Potassium-40 and Calcium-40 (all have mass number 40, but atomic numbers 18, 19 and 20 respectively).

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option C.

 

Additional Information

 

• Isotopes, by contrast, have the same atomic number (same element) but a different mass number (different number of neutrons), e.g. Carbon-12 and Carbon-14.

 

• Isotones are atoms of different elements having the same number of neutrons, e.g. Carbon-14 and Nitrogen-15.

 

NOTE

 

• Total number of electrons (Option A): For neutral atoms, electron count equals the atomic number, so while it does differ, the fundamentally defining property tested here is the atomic number itself.

 

• Total number of nucleons (Option B): This is the mass number, which is, by definition, the same for all isobars — not different.

 

• Mass number (Option D): This is exactly what is kept the same across isobars; it is the identifying similarity, not a difference.

question: Simplify: x^2 − (3x − 2)(x + 5)
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option B i.e. −2x² − 13x + 10.

 

GIVEN

 

• x² − (3x − 2)(x + 5)

 

SOLUTION

 

• Expand (3x − 2)(x + 5) = 3x² + 15x − 2x − 10 = 3x² + 13x − 10.

 

• x² − (3x² + 13x − 10) = x² − 3x² − 13x + 10 = −2x² − 13x + 10.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option B.

 

SHORT TRICK

 

• Expand the bracket first and keep the minus sign outside applied to every term — a common mistake is forgetting to flip the sign of the −10 term.

 

NOTE

 

• Always distribute the outer negative sign to all three terms of the expanded bracket, including the constant.

question: A dealer allowed a 73% discount on an article and was still able to manage a 56% profit. Find the ratio of the cost price to listed price.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option A i.e. 9 : 52.

 

GIVEN

 

• Discount = 73% on marked price (MP); Profit = 56% on cost price (CP).

 

SOLUTION

 

• Selling Price (SP) = MP × (1 − 73/100) = 0.27 × MP.

 

• Also SP = CP × (1 + 56/100) = 1.56 × CP.

 

• Equating: 1.56 × CP = 0.27 × MP ⇒ CP/MP = 0.27/1.56 = 27/156 = 9/52.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option A.

 

SHORT TRICK

 

• CP : MP = (100 − discount%) : (100 + profit%), scaled to lowest terms → 27 : 156 = 9 : 52.

 

NOTE

 

• Never confuse discount% (on MP) with profit% (on CP) — they act on different bases, so equate via SP as the common link.

question: Raju walks to his office 3.5 km away from home. In the morning, he covers the distance in 1.5 hours, whereas, while returning home in the evening, he takes 30 more minutes to cover the same distance. Find his average speed (in km/hr) during the two-way journey.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option C i.e. 2.

 

GIVEN

 

• One-way distance = 3.5 km. Morning time = 1.5 h. Evening time = 1.5 h + 30 min = 2 h.

 

SOLUTION

 

• Total distance (two-way) = 3.5 + 3.5 = 7 km.

 

• Total time taken = 1.5 + 2 = 3.5 h.

 

• Average speed = Total distance ÷ Total time = 7 ÷ 3.5 = 2 km/hr.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option C.

 

SHORT TRICK

 

• For a two-way trip, Average speed = Total distance ÷ Total time — never just the average of the two individual speeds.

 

NOTE

 

• 30 minutes must be converted to 0.5 hour before adding to the morning time; a common slip is treating it as 0.3 h.

question: The marked price of a chair is ₹7,600, which is 25% above the cost price. It is sold at a discount of 4% on the marked price. Find the profit percentage.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option C i.e. 20%.

 

GIVEN

 

• Marked Price (MP) = ₹7,600, which is 25% above Cost Price (CP). Discount on MP = 4%.

 

SOLUTION

 

• CP = MP ÷ 1.25 = 7,600 ÷ 1.25 = ₹6,080.

 

• Selling Price (SP) = MP × (1 − 0.04) = 7,600 × 0.96 = ₹7,296.

 

• Profit = SP − CP = 7,296 − 6,080 = ₹1,216.

 

• Profit% = (1,216 ÷ 6,080) × 100 = 20%.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option C.

 

SHORT TRICK

 

• Net effect of markup m% and discount d% on CP: Profit% = m + d − (m×d)/100 = 25 − 4 − (25×4)/100 = 21 − 1 = 20%.

 

NOTE

 

• Since markup is on CP but discount is on MP, use the combined formula (m + d − md/100), not a simple subtraction of 25% − 4%.

question: If 20% of a number is added to 78, then the result is the same number. 80% of the same number is:
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option D i.e. 78.

 

GIVEN

 

• 78 + 20% of N = N.

 

SOLUTION

 

• 78 + 0.2N = N ⇒ 78 = N − 0.2N = 0.8N.

 

• So 0.8N = 78, i.e. 80% of the number = 78 — this is exactly what is asked.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option D.

 

SHORT TRICK

 

• Notice the equation 78 = 0.8N directly IS '80% of N'; no need to solve for N itself (N = 97.5) — just read off the required value.

 

NOTE

 

• Rearranging 78 + 0.2N = N as N − 0.2N = 78N gives 0.8N = 78 in one step; recognising this shortcut saves solving for N unnecessarily.

question:
If the mean and mode are equal for the given data. Find x (x<6).

Class Interval 15-25 25-35 35-45

Quantity 6 10 x
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option A i.e. 4.

 

GIVEN

 

• Class intervals 15-25, 25-35, 35-45 with frequencies 6, 10, x respectively (x < 6), and Mean = Mode.

 

SOLUTION

 

• Since x < 6 ≤ 10, the class 25-35 (frequency 10) is the modal class: L = 25, f1 = 10, f0 = 6, f2 = x, h = 10.

 

• Mode = L + [(f1 − f0)/(2f1 − f0 − f2)] × h = 25 + [4/(14 − x)] × 10.

 

• Mean = Σfx/Σf, taking midpoints 20, 30, 40: Mean = (6×20 + 10×30 + x×40)/(16 + x) = (420 + 40x)/(16 + x).

 

• Testing x = 4: Mean = (420+160)/20 = 580/20 = 29; Mode = 25 + 40/10 = 25 + 4 = 29. Mean = Mode ✓.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option A.

 

SHORT TRICK

 

• With only 4 whole-number options (x < 6), substitute each candidate value into both the Mean and Mode formulas and pick the one where they match — often faster than solving the equation algebraically.

 

NOTE

 

• Always identify the correct modal class first (the one with the highest frequency) before applying the mode formula.

question: The product of two consecutive odd numbers is 16383. Which is the smaller one?
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option D i.e. 127.

 

GIVEN

 

• Two consecutive odd numbers, say n and (n + 2), whose product = 16383.

 

SOLUTION

 

• n(n + 2) = 16383 ⇒ n² + 2n − 16383 = 0.

 

• Using the quadratic formula: n = [−2 + √(4 + 4×16383)]/2 = [−2 + √65536]/2 = (−2 + 256)/2 = 254/2 = 127.

 

• Check: 127 × 129 = 16383 ✓. So the numbers are 127 and 129; the smaller one is 127.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option D.

 

SHORT TRICK

 

• √16383 ≈ 128 (since 128² = 16384, just 1 more than 16383), so the two consecutive odd numbers straddling 128 are 127 and 129 — verify by multiplying.

 

NOTE

 

• For 'product of two consecutive (odd/even) numbers' questions, estimate √(product) first — the two numbers will be just below and above that estimate.

question: A fruit seller purchases lemons at 2 for a rupee and sells them at 5 for three rupees. Find his profit percentage.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option D i.e. 20.

 

GIVEN

 

• Cost price: 2 lemons for ₹1. Selling price: 5 lemons for ₹3.

 

SOLUTION

 

• CP per lemon = 1/2 = ₹0.5. SP per lemon = 3/5 = ₹0.6.

 

• Profit per lemon = 0.6 − 0.5 = ₹0.1.

 

• Profit% = (Profit/CP) × 100 = (0.1/0.5) × 100 = 20%.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option D.

 

SHORT TRICK

 

• Take LCM of 2 and 5 = 10 lemons: CP of 10 = ₹5, SP of 10 = 2 × 3 = ₹6. Profit% = (1/5) × 100 = 20%.

 

NOTE

 

• Always convert 'X for ₹Y' statements to a per-unit CP/SP (or use a common LCM quantity) before comparing.

question: If the ratio of two numbers is 7 : 8, and their HCF is 32, then their LCM is:
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option C i.e. 1792.

 

GIVEN

 

• Ratio of numbers = 7 : 8; HCF = 32.

 

SOLUTION

 

• Since the ratio is in lowest terms, the numbers are 7 × 32 = 224 and 8 × 32 = 256.

 

• LCM = Product of numbers ÷ HCF = (224 × 256) ÷ 32 = 224 × 8 = 1792.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option C.

 

SHORT TRICK

 

• When two numbers are in ratio a : b (lowest terms) with HCF = h, LCM = a × b × h directly = 7 × 8 × 32 = 1792.

 

NOTE

 

• LCM × HCF = Product of the two numbers — this identity is the fastest route whenever the ratio and HCF are both given.

question: 6 men can complete a piece of work in 5 days while 2 women can do it in 15 days. In how many days can 3 women and 3 men complete it?
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option C i.e. 5 days.

 

GIVEN

 

• 6 men finish the work in 5 days; 2 women finish the same work in 15 days.

 

SOLUTION

 

• Total work = 6 men × 5 days = 30 man-days ⇒ 1 man's 1-day work = 1/30.

 

• Total work = 2 women × 15 days = 30 woman-days ⇒ 1 woman's 1-day work = 1/30 (same rate as a man here).

 

• Combined 1-day work of 3 women + 3 men = 3(1/30) + 3(1/30) = 6/30 = 1/5.

 

• So the work is completed in 5 days.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option C.

 

SHORT TRICK

 

• Express both given conditions as total man-days/woman-days (=30 in each case) — this reveals 1 woman's rate equals 1 man's rate here, simplifying the combined calculation.

 

NOTE

 

• Always convert 'work done in N days by K people' into total (person × days) units — this is the fastest way to compare men's and women's efficiencies.

question: Three numbers are in the ratio 17 : 12 : 6 and the sum of these numbers is 1820. Find the middle number.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option B i.e. 624.

 

GIVEN

 

• Three numbers in ratio 17 : 12 : 6; sum = 1820.

 

SOLUTION

 

• Total parts = 17 + 12 + 6 = 35 parts = 1820 ⇒ 1 part = 1820 ÷ 35 = 52.

 

• The numbers are 17 × 52 = 884, 12 × 52 = 624, and 6 × 52 = 312.

 

• The middle number (by value) is 624.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option B.

 

SHORT TRICK

 

• Find the value of '1 part' first (sum ÷ total parts), then multiply by each ratio term — here, the middle ratio term (12) directly gives the middle number.

 

NOTE

 

• Double-check which ratio term is actually the 'middle' value once multiplied out; ratio order doesn't always match numeric order, though here it does (884 > 624 > 312).

question: A five digit number 761xy is divisible by 90. Find (x + y).
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option D i.e. 4.

 

GIVEN

 

• The number 761xy is divisible by 90 = 9 × 10.

 

SOLUTION

 

• Divisibility by 10 ⇒ the last digit y must be 0.

 

• Divisibility by 9 ⇒ sum of digits (7+6+1+x+y) must be a multiple of 9: 14 + x + 0 = 14 + x.

 

• The smallest multiple of 9 ≥ 14 is 18, so x = 18 − 14 = 4.

 

• So x = 4, y = 0, and x + y = 4.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option D.

 

SHORT TRICK

 

• For divisibility by 90, fix the units digit as 0 first (from the '10' factor), then apply the digit-sum rule for 9 to the remaining unknown.

 

NOTE

 

• 90 = 9 × 10 (co-prime factors), so a number divisible by 90 must independently satisfy the divisibility rules for both 9 and 10.

question: Pushpraj and Himani together invested ₹34,100 in a business. At the end of the year, out of a total profit of ₹5,400, Pushpraj's share was ₹2,700. What was the investment of Pushpraj?
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option D i.e. ₹17,050.

 

GIVEN

 

• Total investment = ₹34,100. Total profit = ₹5,400, of which Pushpraj's share = ₹2,700.

 

SOLUTION

 

• In a partnership (same time period for both), profit share is directly proportional to investment.

 

• Pushpraj's share of profit = 2,700/5,400 = 1/2 of the total profit.

 

• So Pushpraj's investment must also be 1/2 of the total investment = (1/2) × 34,100 = ₹17,050.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option D.

 

SHORT TRICK

 

• Profit ratio = Investment ratio (for equal time). Since Pushpraj got exactly half the profit, he also invested exactly half the total capital.

 

NOTE

 

• This works only because the profit-sharing ratio equals exactly 1 : 1 here; in general, always find the profit-share fraction first, then apply it to total investment.

question: A ladder is leaning against a wall, making an angle of 60° with the ground. If the foot of the ladder is 5 m away from the wall, find the length of the ladder.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option D i.e. 10 m.

 

GIVEN

 

• Angle with the ground = 60°. Distance of foot of ladder from wall (base) = 5 m.

 

SOLUTION

 

• Let the ladder's length be L. The base (5 m) is adjacent to the 60° angle, and L is the hypotenuse.

 

• cos 60° = base/hypotenuse = 5/L ⇒ L = 5/cos 60° = 5/(1/2) = 10 m.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option D.

 

SHORT TRICK

 

• cos 60° = 1/2 is a standard value — dividing the base by 1/2 (i.e. doubling it) instantly gives the hypotenuse: 5 × 2 = 10 m.

 

NOTE

 

• Memorise standard trig ratios for 30°, 45°, 60° — they turn most ladder/height-distance questions into one-line calculations.

question:
Simplify the following:

(5^(3x+4) + 125^(x+1)) / (125^(x+1) − 5^(3x+2))
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option A i.e. 7.5.

 

GIVEN

 

• Expression: (5^(3x+4) + 125^(x+1)) ÷ (125^(x+1) − 5^(3x+2)).

 

SOLUTION

 

• Rewrite 125 as 5³, so 125^(x+1) = 5^(3x+3).

 

• Numerator = 5^(3x+4) + 5^(3x+3) = 5^(3x+3)(5 + 1) = 6 × 5^(3x+3).

 

• Denominator = 5^(3x+3) − 5^(3x+2) = 5^(3x+2)(5 − 1) = 4 × 5^(3x+2).

 

• Ratio = [6 × 5^(3x+3)] / [4 × 5^(3x+2)] = (6/4) × 5^((3x+3)−(3x+2)) = 1.5 × 5¹ = 7.5.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option A.

 

SHORT TRICK

 

• Always express every term with the same base (here, base 5) first, then factor out the smallest power to simplify the ratio quickly.

 

NOTE

 

• Keep careful track of exponent arithmetic (3x+3, 3x+2, etc.) — a sign slip here is the most common source of error in such index-based simplifications.

question: A and B working together can do a piece of work in 4 days. B alone can do the same work in 20 days. How long (in days) will A alone take to do double the work?
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option D i.e. 10.

 

GIVEN

 

• (A + B) together finish the work in 4 days. B alone finishes it in 20 days.

 

SOLUTION

 

• (A + B)'s 1-day work = 1/4. B's 1-day work = 1/20.

 

• A's 1-day work = 1/4 − 1/20 = 5/20 − 1/20 = 4/20 = 1/5.

 

• So A alone takes 5 days to finish the work once.

 

• To do double the work, A will take 2 × 5 = 10 days.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option D.

 

SHORT TRICK

 

• Find A's single-work time first (1/A = 1/4 − 1/20 ⇒ A = 5 days), then simply double it for double the work — time is directly proportional to the amount of work at a fixed rate.

 

NOTE

 

• Don't confuse 'double the work' with 'double the rate' — a fixed worker takes proportionally more time for more work, not less.

question: In quadrilateral PQRS, the bisectors of ∠R and ∠S meet at the point T (inside the quadrilateral) and ∠STR = 13.5°. If the ratio of ∠P to ∠Q is 4 : 5, then what is the difference between the measures of ∠Q and ∠P?
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option C i.e. 3°.

 

GIVEN

 

• ∠STR = 13.5° (angle between bisectors of ∠R and ∠S). ∠P : ∠Q = 4 : 5.

 

SOLUTION

 

• Standard result: if the bisectors of two angles (R, S) of a quadrilateral meet at T, then ∠RTS = ½(∠P + ∠Q).

 

• So ½(∠P + ∠Q) = 13.5° ⇒ ∠P + ∠Q = 27°.

 

• With ∠P : ∠Q = 4 : 5 (9 parts = 27°, 1 part = 3°): ∠P = 4 × 3 = 12°, ∠Q = 5 × 3 = 15°.

 

• Difference = ∠Q − ∠P = 15° − 12° = 3°.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option C.

 

SHORT TRICK

 

• Memorise the identity: angle between bisectors of two angles of a quadrilateral = half the sum of the other two angles — it converts the whole problem into simple ratio-splitting.

 

NOTE

 

• Derivation: in triangle RTS, ∠TRS = R/2, ∠TSR = S/2, so ∠RTS = 180° − (R+S)/2; since R+S = 360° − (P+Q), this simplifies exactly to (P+Q)/2.

question: The arithmetic mean of the observations 42, 97, 57, 62, 52, 13, 44, 23 and 69 is:
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option A i.e. 51.

 

GIVEN

 

• Observations: 42, 97, 57, 62, 52, 13, 44, 23, 69 (9 values).

 

SOLUTION

 

• Sum = 42+97+57+62+52+13+44+23+69 = 459.

 

• Number of observations = 9.

 

• Mean = 459 ÷ 9 = 51.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option A.

 

SHORT TRICK

 

• Pair numbers that sum to round values while adding: (42+58≈)... or simply add sequentially in groups of 3: (42+97+57)=196, (62+52+13)=127, (44+23+69)=136; total = 196+127+136 = 459.

 

NOTE

 

• Arithmetic mean = (Sum of all observations) ÷ (Number of observations); always recount the number of terms carefully before dividing.

question: The ratio of the present ages of two cousins is 3 : 2. After 6 years, the ratio will become 5 : 4. What was the sum of their ages (in years) 4 years ago?
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option D i.e. 7.

 

GIVEN

 

• Present ages in ratio 3 : 2. After 6 years, ratio becomes 5 : 4.

 

SOLUTION

 

• Let present ages = 3x and 2x.

 

• After 6 years: (3x + 6)/(2x + 6) = 5/4 ⇒ 4(3x + 6) = 5(2x + 6) ⇒ 12x + 24 = 10x + 30 ⇒ 2x = 6 ⇒ x = 3.

 

• Present ages: 3(3) = 9 years and 2(3) = 6 years. Sum now = 15 years.

 

• Sum 4 years ago = 15 − (4 + 4) = 15 − 8 = 7 years.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option D.

 

SHORT TRICK

 

• Once present sum is known, the sum 'n years ago' for two people simply reduces by 2n (n years each): 15 − 2(4) = 7.

 

NOTE

 

• Always solve for the ratio multiplier (x) first using the future-ratio condition, then compute present ages before adjusting for past/future years.

question: The salary of a person was decreased by 30% and subsequently increased by 30% for 2 years. What is the percentage change in the salary?
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option C i.e. Increase of 18.3%.

 

GIVEN

 

• Salary first decreased by 30%, then increased by 30% for each of the next 2 years (i.e., a +30% change applied twice).

 

SOLUTION

 

• Let initial salary = 100.

 

• After decrease of 30%: 100 × 0.70 = 70.

 

• After 1st year's 30% increase: 70 × 1.30 = 91.

 

• After 2nd year's 30% increase: 91 × 1.30 = 118.3.

 

• Net change = 118.3 − 100 = +18.3%, i.e. an increase of 18.3%.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option C.

 

SHORT TRICK

 

• Chain successive percentage changes by multiplying factors: 0.70 × 1.30 × 1.30 = 1.183 → +18.3% overall.

 

NOTE

 

• Never simply add/subtract percentages like −30+30+30=30%; successive percentage changes must always be multiplied as factors, not added.

question: Find the area of a triangle whose sides are in the ratio 28 : 23 : 35 and its perimeter is 516 cm.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option C i.e. 720√258 cm².

 

GIVEN

 

• Sides in ratio 28 : 23 : 35; perimeter = 516 cm.

 

SOLUTION

 

• Sum of ratio parts = 28 + 23 + 35 = 86 parts = 516 cm ⇒ 1 part = 6 cm.

 

• Sides = 168 cm, 138 cm, 210 cm. Semi-perimeter s = 516/2 = 258 cm.

 

• By Heron's formula: Area = √[s(s−a)(s−b)(s−c)] = √[258 × (258−168) × (258−138) × (258−210)] = √[258 × 90 × 120 × 48].

 

• 258 × 90 × 120 × 48 = 133,747,200 = 2⁹ × 3⁵ × 5² × 43 = (2⁴ × 3² × 5)² × (2 × 3 × 43) = 720² × 258.

 

• So Area = 720√258 cm².

 

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option C.

 

SHORT TRICK

 

• After finding s and the three (s−side) values, factor the product into a perfect square × a small remainder — pull the perfect square root outside the radical instead of estimating √(big number) directly.

 

NOTE

 

• Heron's formula Area = √[s(s−a)(s−b)(s−c)] is the go-to method whenever only the three sides (or their ratio + perimeter) are given, with no angle information.

question: The cost of a washing machine is 50% less than the cost of a TV. If the cost of the washing machine increases by 83% and that of the TV decreases by 38%, then what is the percentage change in the total cost of 8 washing machines and 4 TVs?
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option B i.e. Increase by 22.5%.

 

GIVEN

 

• Washing machine (WM) cost = 50% less than TV (T), so WM = T/2. WM increases by 83%; TV decreases by 38%.

 

SOLUTION

 

• Old total cost = 8 × WM + 4 × T = 8 × (T/2) + 4T = 4T + 4T = 8T.

 

• New WM = 0.5T × 1.83 = 0.915T. New TV = T × 0.62 = 0.62T.

 

• New total cost = 8 × 0.915T + 4 × 0.62T = 7.32T + 2.48T = 9.8T.

 

• % change = (9.8T − 8T)/8T × 100 = 1.8T/8T × 100 = 22.5% increase.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option B.

 

SHORT TRICK

 

• Express everything in terms of TV price T only (since WM = T/2), reducing the whole problem to a single-variable percentage comparison.

 

NOTE

 

• Always compute the OLD total and NEW total separately in the same variable before taking the percentage change — mixing WM-based and TV-based units directly leads to errors.

question: The perimeter (in cm) of a right-angled triangle whose sides that make the right angle are 18 cm and 24 cm, is:
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option A i.e. 72.

 

GIVEN

 

• The two legs (sides forming the right angle) = 18 cm and 24 cm.

 

SOLUTION

 

• Hypotenuse = √(18² + 24²) = √(324 + 576) = √900 = 30 cm.

 

• Perimeter = 18 + 24 + 30 = 72 cm.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option A.

 

SHORT TRICK

 

• 18 : 24 = 3 : 4 (scaled by 6), so this is a scaled-up 3-4-5 Pythagorean triplet: 3×6, 4×6, 5×6 = 18, 24, 30 — hypotenuse follows instantly without computing squares.

 

NOTE

 

• Recognising common triplets (3-4-5, 5-12-13, 8-15-17) in scaled form is one of the fastest tricks for right-triangle questions.

question: What would the annual interest accrued on a deposit of ₹3,500 in a bank that pays a 17% per annum rate of simple interest be?
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option A i.e. ₹595.

 

GIVEN

 

• Principal P = ₹3,500. Rate R = 17% per annum. Time T = 1 year.

 

SOLUTION

 

• Simple Interest = (P × R × T)/100 = (3,500 × 17 × 1)/100.

 

• = 3,500 × 0.17 = ₹595.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option A.

 

SHORT TRICK

 

• 17% of 3,500 = 10% (350) + 5% (175) + 2% (70) = 350+175+70 = 595 — break the percentage into easy chunks (10%, 5%, 2%) for quick mental calculation.

 

NOTE

 

• For T = 1 year, Simple Interest = P × R/100 directly, since T drops out — no separate compounding to worry about.

question: A train 1439 m long is running at 36 km/hr. How long will it take to clear a 1331 m long platform completely?
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option C i.e. 277 seconds.

 

GIVEN

 

• Train length = 1439 m. Speed = 36 km/hr. Platform length = 1331 m.

 

SOLUTION

 

• Convert speed to m/s: 36 × (5/18) = 10 m/s.

 

• To clear the platform completely, the train must cover its own length + the platform's length: 1439 + 1331 = 2770 m.

 

• Time = Distance ÷ Speed = 2770 ÷ 10 = 277 seconds.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option C.

 

SHORT TRICK

 

• To convert km/hr to m/s, multiply by 5/18 (a value worth memorising); to 'clear' any obstacle, always add train length + obstacle length.

 

NOTE

 

• A common mistake is using only the platform length (1331 m) or only the train length, instead of their sum, as the distance to be covered.

question:
Based on the English alphabetical order, three of the following four letter-cluster pairs are alike in a certain way and thus form a group. Which letter-cluster pair DOES NOT belong to that group?

(Note: The odd one out is not based on the number of consonants/vowels or their position in the letter-cluster.)
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option D i.e. JM-GL.

 

GIVEN

 

• Four letter-cluster pairs: NQ-KO, LO-IM, PS-MQ, JM-GL.

 

SOLUTION

 

• Convert letters to their positions (A=1...Z=26) and find the difference between the two clusters, letter by letter.

 

• NQ(14,17)-KO(11,15): differences = 14−11=3, 17−15=2 → pattern (−3, −2).

 

• LO(12,15)-IM(9,13): differences = 12−9=3, 15−13=2 → pattern (−3, −2).

 

• PS(16,19)-MQ(13,17): differences = 16−13=3, 19−17=2 → pattern (−3, −2).

 

• JM(10,13)-GL(7,12): differences = 10−7=3, 13−12=1 → pattern (−3, −1) — breaks the pattern.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option D.

 

SHORT TRICK

 

• Convert each pair to numbers and check the per-letter difference between the two clusters — three pairs will share the identical difference pattern; the odd one out won't.

 

NOTE

 

• Always check BOTH letters' differences, not just the first — the first letter's gap can match while the second letter's gap breaks the pattern, as seen here (JM-GL).

question: In a certain code language, 'VAIL' is coded as '6598' and 'OVAL' is coded as '8619'. What is the code for 'O' in the given code language?
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option C i.e. 1.

 

GIVEN

 

• VAIL → 6598, OVAL → 8619.

 

SOLUTION

 

• Letters of VAIL {V, A, I, L} map to the digit set {6, 5, 9, 8}. Letters of OVAL {O, V, A, L} map to the digit set {8, 6, 1, 9}.

 

• The letters common to both words are V, A and L, so their codes must be the digits common to both digit sets: {6, 5, 9, 8} ∩ {8, 6, 1, 9} = {6, 8, 9}.

 

• The letter I appears only in VAIL, so its code is the digit present in VAIL's set but not OVAL's: that is 5.

 

• The letter O appears only in OVAL, so its code is the digit present in OVAL's set but not VAIL's: that is 1.

 

• So O = 1.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option C.

 

SHORT TRICK

 

• List the digit set for each coded word; the digit(s) that appear in only ONE of the two sets must belong to the letter(s) unique to that word — no need to solve for every letter individually.

 

NOTE

 

• This method (set difference of digits ↔ set difference of letters) is much faster than trying to fix a letter-to-digit position mapping, which can be misleading here since V, A, L don't sit in matching positions across the two words.

question:
What should come in place of the question mark (?) in the given series?

 

99 87 75 63 51 ?
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option A i.e. 39.

 

GIVEN

 

• Series: 99, 87, 75, 63, 51, ?

 

SOLUTION

 

• Find the differences between consecutive terms: 87−99=−12, 75−87=−12, 63−75=−12, 51−63=−12.

 

• The series decreases by a constant 12 each time.

 

• Next term = 51 − 12 = 39.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option A.

 

SHORT TRICK

 

• Whenever consecutive differences are constant, it's a simple arithmetic progression — just extend the pattern by the same common difference.

 

NOTE

 

• Always verify the common difference across at least 3-4 consecutive pairs before extending the series, to rule out a more complex (e.g. alternating) pattern.

question: Seven people, B, C, D, I, J, K and L, are sitting around a circular table facing the centre of the table. L sits third to the left of I. Only one person sits between K and B when counted from the left of B. C sits third to the right of D. J is not an immediate neighbour of L. How many people sit between J and B when counted from the right of J?
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option B i.e. Three.

 

GIVEN

 

• L is third to the left of I. Only one person sits between K and B (counted from left of B). C is third to the right of D. J is not an immediate neighbour of L.

 

SOLUTION

 

• Use clockwise positions 0-6, taking 'left' = +1 step clockwise. Fix I = 0, so L (third to the left of I) = 3.

 

• 'Only one person between K and B, counted from left of B' means K is 2 seats clockwise from B: K = B + 2.

 

• Testing B = 2 gives K = 4 (both free seats). The remaining seats {1, 5, 6} go to C, D, J, with the condition C = D − 3 (C third to the right of D, i.e. 3 steps counter-clockwise).

 

• Among {1, 5, 6}: taking D = 1 gives C = 1 − 3 = −2 ≡ 5 (mod 7), which is free — so D = 1, C = 5, leaving J = 6.

 

• Check: J(6) is not adjacent to L(3) — neighbours of L are 2 and 4, so this is satisfied. Final seats (clockwise from I=0): I, D, B, L, K, C, J.

 

• 'Counted from the right of J' means moving counter-clockwise from J(6): 6→5(C)→4(K)→3(L)→2(B). Between J and B lie C, K and L — 3 people.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option B.

 

SHORT TRICK

 

• In circular seating puzzles with mixed 'left of X' and 'right of Y' clues, fix ONE person as your reference point (position 0) and convert every other clue into a signed offset from that reference before placing anyone else.

 

NOTE

 

• Always verify the final arrangement against every given clue (including negative/exclusion clues like 'J is not an immediate neighbour of L') before reading off the answer — this arrangement satisfies all five conditions.

question: In a row of people all facing north, Aftab is 18th from the right end. Apoorva is 28th from the right end. Apoorva is exactly between Aftab and Piyali. If Piyali is 12th from the left end of the line, how many people are there in the row?
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option D i.e. 49.

 

GIVEN

 

• Aftab = 18th from right. Apoorva = 28th from right. Piyali = 12th from left. Apoorva is exactly midway between Aftab and Piyali.

 

SOLUTION

 

• Let total people = N. Position from left = (N + 1) − position from right.

 

• Aftab's position from left = N + 1 − 18 = N − 17. Apoorva's position from left = N + 1 − 28 = N − 27.

 

• Since Apoorva is exactly midway between Aftab and Piyali (position 12 from left): (N − 27) = [(N − 17) + 12]/2.

 

• 2(N − 27) = (N − 17) + 12 ⇒ 2N − 54 = N − 5 ⇒ N = 49.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option D.

 

SHORT TRICK

 

• Convert every 'position from right' clue into 'position from left' using (N + 1 − position from right) as soon as possible — this lets all clues be compared on the same scale.

 

NOTE

 

• 'Exactly between' means the midpoint condition: middle position = average of the two end positions — set up this equation directly instead of guessing.

question: A, B, C, D, W, X and Y are sitting around a circular table facing the centre of the table. A sits fourth to the left of Y. W sits fourth to the right of C. Only two people sit between Y and C when counted from the left of Y. X is not an immediate neighbour of W or Y. D is not an immediate neighbour of X. Who sits third to the right of B?
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option B i.e. D.

 

GIVEN

 

• A is 4th to the left of Y. W is 4th to the right of C. Only two people sit between Y and C (counted from left of Y). X is not adjacent to W or Y. D is not adjacent to X.

 

SOLUTION

 

• Fix Y at position 0 (clockwise numbering, 'left' = +1 direction). Then A = Y + 4 = 4.

 

• 'Two people between Y and C counted from left of Y' means C = Y + 3 = 3.

 

• W is 4th to the right of C (i.e. −4 direction): W = C − 4 = 3 − 4 = −1 ≡ 6 (mod 7).

 

• Remaining seats {1, 2, 5} are for B, D, X. Since X can't be adjacent to W(6) or Y(0) — i.e. X ≠ 1 and X ≠ 5 — the only option is X = 2.

 

• D can't be adjacent to X(2), i.e. D ≠ 1 (3 is already C). So D = 5, leaving B = 1.

 

• Final order (clockwise from Y=0): Y, B, X, C, A, D, W.

 

• 'Third to the right' of B(1) means moving 3 steps in the −1 (right) direction: 1 − 3 = −2 ≡ 5 (mod 7), which is D.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option B.

 

SHORT TRICK

 

• Convert all 'left of'/'right of' clues into a single consistent numeric direction (e.g., left = +1, right = −1) around a fixed 0–6 clock face — this avoids confusion when clues mix directions.

 

NOTE

 

• Apply exclusion clues (X and D's non-adjacency conditions) only after placing all clues with definite offsets — they are best used to eliminate ambiguity in the last remaining seats.

question:
What should come in place of the question mark (?) in the given series?

 

621 623 627 633 641 ?
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option D i.e. 651.

 

GIVEN

 

• Series: 621, 623, 627, 633, 641, ?

 

SOLUTION

 

• Differences between consecutive terms: 623−621=2, 627−623=4, 633−627=6, 641−633=8.

 

• The differences themselves form a series: 2, 4, 6, 8 — increasing by 2 each time.

 

• Next difference = 10, so next term = 641 + 10 = 651.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option D.

 

SHORT TRICK

 

• Whenever the first differences form their own simple arithmetic pattern (here, consecutive even numbers), extend that pattern one more step before adding it to the last term.

 

NOTE

 

• Always write out the difference row explicitly beneath the series — it makes second-order (difference-of-differences) patterns immediately visible.

question:
Refer to the following number series and answer the question that follows (all numbers are single-digit numbers only). (Counting to be done from left to right only.)

 

(Left) 1 9 6 4 8 8 9 8 7 7 6 5 8 3 4 3 7 5 9 1 5 2 7 1 1 5 9 (Right)

 

How many such even numbers are there each of which is immediately preceded by an odd number and also immediately followed by an odd number?
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option D i.e. 5.

 

GIVEN

 

• Series: 1 9 6 4 8 8 9 8 7 7 6 5 8 3 4 3 7 5 9 1 5 2 7 1 1 5 9 (27 terms).

 

SOLUTION

 

• Scan the series looking for an even digit with an odd digit immediately before AND immediately after it.

 

• Position 8 (value 8): preceded by 9 (odd) ✓, followed by 7 (odd) ✓ — counts.

 

• Position 11 (value 6): preceded by 7 (odd) ✓, followed by 5 (odd) ✓ — counts.

 

• Position 13 (value 8): preceded by 5 (odd) ✓, followed by 3 (odd) ✓ — counts.

 

• Position 15 (value 4): preceded by 3 (odd) ✓, followed by 3 (odd) ✓ — counts.

 

• Position 22 (value 2): preceded by 5 (odd) ✓, followed by 7 (odd) ✓ — counts.

 

• All other even digits fail the test (either the digit before or after is also even). Total qualifying even numbers = 5.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option D.

 

SHORT TRICK

 

• Underline every even digit first, then check only its immediate left and right neighbour — this two-step scan is faster than re-reading the whole series repeatedly.

 

NOTE

 

• The very first and last digits of a series can never qualify for such 'preceded by / followed by' conditions since they have no neighbour on one side.

question:
Refer to the following number series and answer the question that follows (all numbers are single-digit numbers only). Counting to be done from left to right only.

 

(Left) 1 3 5 2 7 1 9 5 1 7 8 4 2 5 7 6 6 5 3 4 7 2 1 7 7 4 9 (Right)

 

How many such odd numbers are there, each of which is immediately preceded by an odd number and also immediately followed by an even number?
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option D i.e. Five.

 

GIVEN

 

• Series: 1 3 5 2 7 1 9 5 1 7 8 4 2 5 7 6 6 5 3 4 7 2 1 7 7 4 9 (27 terms).

 

SOLUTION

 

• Scan for an odd digit with an odd digit immediately before it AND an even digit immediately after it.

 

• Position 3 (value 5): preceded by 3 (odd) ✓, followed by 2 (even) ✓ — counts.

 

• Position 10 (value 7): preceded by 1 (odd) ✓, followed by 8 (even) ✓ — counts.

 

• Position 15 (value 7): preceded by 5 (odd) ✓, followed by 6 (even) ✓ — counts.

 

• Position 19 (value 3): preceded by 5 (odd) ✓, followed by 4 (even) ✓ — counts.

 

• Position 25 (value 7): preceded by 7 (odd) ✓, followed by 4 (even) ✓ — counts.

 

• All other odd digits fail this specific pattern. Total qualifying odd numbers = 5 (Five).

 

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option D.

 

SHORT TRICK

 

• First mark all odd digits, then only check pairs of neighbours around each — separating 'preceded by odd' and 'followed by even' into two quick checks avoids errors.

 

NOTE

 

• Read the condition carefully: 'preceded by odd AND followed by even' is different from 'preceded by odd AND followed by odd' (as in a similar-looking question) — always match the exact wording.

question:
Refer to the following number and symbol series and answer the question that follows. Counting to be done from left to right only. All numbers are single-digit numbers.

 

(Left) # € % # 6 4 * 9 6 @ 5 % @ # © 8 # % * £ 2 (Right)

 

How many such numbers are there each of which is immediately preceded by a symbol and also immediately followed by a symbol?
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option C i.e. 4.

 

GIVEN

 

• Series: # € % # 6 4 * 9 6 @ 5 % @ # © 8 # % * £ 2 (20 terms; #, €, %, *, @, © and £ are symbols; 6, 4, 9, 5, 8, 2 are numbers).

 

SOLUTION

 

• Scan for a number with a symbol immediately before AND immediately after it.

 

• Position 5 (value 6): preceded by # (symbol) ✓, followed by 4 (number) ✗ — fails.

 

• Position 9 (value 6): preceded by * (symbol) ✓, followed by @ (symbol) ✓ — counts.

 

• Position 11 (value 5): preceded by @ (symbol) ✓, followed by % (symbol) ✓ — counts.

 

• Position 16 (value 8): preceded by © (symbol) ✓, followed by # (symbol) ✓ — counts.

 

• Position 20 (value 2): preceded by £ (symbol) ✓, followed by nothing (end of series) — fails.

 

• Re-checking all remaining numbers (4, 9) confirms they don't satisfy both conditions. Total qualifying numbers = 4.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option C.

 

SHORT TRICK

 

• List out only the numeric positions first, then check just their immediate neighbours — this is much faster than scanning the full mixed series repeatedly.

 

NOTE

 

• The first and last elements of the series can never satisfy a 'preceded by AND followed by' condition, since one side has no neighbour.

question:
In a certain code language,

P @ Q means 'P is the husband of Q',

P # Q means 'P is the brother of Q',

P & Q means 'P is the mother of Q', and

P % Q means 'P is the sister of Q'.

 

Based on the above, how is D related to E if 'D # S @ Z & M % E'?
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option C i.e. Father's brother.

 

GIVEN

 

• D # S → D is the brother of S.

 

• S @ Z → S is the husband of Z.

 

• Z & M → Z is the mother of M.

 

• M % E → M is the sister of E.

 

SOLUTION

 

• S is the husband of Z, and Z is the mother of M, so S is the father of M.

 

• M is the sister of E, so S is also the father of E.

 

• D is the brother of S, and S is E's father, so D is the brother of E's father, i.e. D is E's father's brother.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option C.

 

SHORT TRICK

 

• Redraw the code chain as a family tree step by step (D–S, S–Z, Z–M, M–E) before naming the final relation; this avoids losing track of generations.

 

NOTE

 

• Since M and E are sisters and S is M's father, S is also E's father — a step test-takers often miss.

question:
Which of the following letter-number clusters will replace the question mark (?) in the given series to make it logically complete?

 

QIS38, SLQ42, UOO46, ?
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option B i.e. WRM50.

 

GIVEN

 

• Series: QIS38, SLQ42, UOO46, ?

 

SOLUTION

 

• 1st letters: Q(17), S(19), U(21) → increasing by +2 each time → next = W(23).

 

• 2nd letters: I(9), L(12), O(15) → increasing by +3 each time → next = R(18).

 

• 3rd letters: S(19), Q(17), O(15) → decreasing by −2 each time → next = M(13).

 

• Numbers: 38, 42, 46 → increasing by +4 each time → next = 50.

 

• Combining: W, R, M, 50 → WRM50.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option B.

 

SHORT TRICK

 

• Split a letter-number cluster series into separate columns (1st letters, 2nd letters, 3rd letters, numbers) and find the pattern in each column independently — most such series use simple constant-difference patterns per column.

 

NOTE

 

• Watch for columns moving in opposite directions (here the 3rd letter column decreases while the others increase) — don't assume all columns follow the same trend.

question:
In the following triads, each group of letters is related to the subsequent one following a certain logic. Select from the given options, the one which follows the same logic.

GIFT - IFGT - TFIG

LAND - ANLD - DNAL
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option D i.e. FLAG - LAFG - GALF.

 

GIVEN

 

• GIFT → IFGT → TFIG, and LAND → ANLD → DNAL both follow the same hidden logic.

 

SOLUTION

 

• Step 1 (word1 → word2): rotate the first three letters left by one place, keep the 4th letter fixed. GIFT: G,I,F → I,F,G, so GIFT → IFGT ✓. LAND: L,A,N → A,N,L, so LAND → ANLD ✓.

 

• Step 2 (word2 → word3): rearrange as [letter4, letter2, letter1, letter3]. IFGT(I,F,G,T) → (T,F,I,G) = TFIG ✓. ANLD(A,N,L,D) → (D,N,A,L) = DNAL ✓.

 

• Apply both steps to FLAG: Step 1 — F,L,A → L,A,F, giving FLAG → LAFG (matches the given word2 form exactly).

 

• Step 2 on LAFG(L,A,F,G) → [G,A,L,F] = GALF (matches the given word3 form exactly).

 

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option D.

 

SHORT TRICK

 

• Number the letters 1-2-3-4 in the first word and track exactly which position each letter moves to in word2, then word3 — apply the identical positional rule to each option's first word to test it.

 

NOTE

 

• Test only the FIRST transformation (word1→word2) initially to quickly eliminate options that don't even match that step, before checking the second transformation.

question:
Which of the following letter-number clusters will replace the question mark (?) in the given series to make it logically complete?

 

MEW154, SKC131, YQI108, EWO85, ?
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option B i.e. KCU62.

 

GIVEN

 

• Series: MEW154, SKC131, YQI108, EWO85, ?

 

SOLUTION

 

• 1st letters: M(13), S(19), Y(25), E(31→ wraps to 5 after Z), and continuing +6 each step: 5+6=11=K.

 

• 2nd letters: E(5), K(11), Q(17), W(23), next +6 = 29→ wraps to 29−26=3=C.

 

• 3rd letters: W(23), C(3, after wrap from 29), I(9), O(15), next +6 = 21=U.

 

• Numbers: 154, 131, 108, 85 — decreasing by 23 each time: 85 − 23 = 62.

 

• Combining: K, C, U, 62 → KCU62.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option B.

 

SHORT TRICK

 

• Split into letter columns and a number column separately; letters here increase by a fixed step (+6) with wrap-around past Z, while the number decreases by a fixed step (−23) — treat wrap-around as (position − 26) once it exceeds 26.

 

NOTE

 

• Always double check wrap-around arithmetic (position mod 26) carefully — this is the most common source of error in alphabet-position series.

question: If each of the digits in the number 243178569 is arranged in descending order from left to right, then what will be the sum of the digits which are second from the right and third from the left in the new number thus formed?
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option D i.e. 9.

 

GIVEN

 

• Number: 243178569 (digits: 2,4,3,1,7,8,5,6,9).

 

SOLUTION

 

• Arrange all 9 digits in descending order: 9 8 7 6 5 4 3 2 1.

 

• Second digit from the right: that's the 8th digit from the left, which is 2.

 

• Third digit from the left: that's 7.

 

• Sum = 2 + 7 = 9.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option D.

 

SHORT TRICK

 

• After rearranging in descending order (a straightforward sort of the 9 given digits), simply count positions directly from each end — no need to re-derive the whole number each time.

 

NOTE

 

• 'Second from the right' in a 9-digit number is the same as the '8th digit from the left' (position = total digits + 1 − position from right).

question:
If + means −, − means ×, × means ÷ and ÷ means +, then what will come in place of the question mark (?) in the following equation?

 

113 − 9 ÷ 17 + 519 × 3 = ?
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option D i.e. 861.

 

GIVEN

 

• Symbol swap: + means −, − means ×, × means ÷, ÷ means +. Expression: 113 − 9 ÷ 17 + 519 × 3.

 

SOLUTION

 

• Replace each symbol with its actual meaning: '−' becomes '×', '÷' becomes '+', '+' becomes '−', '×' becomes '÷'.

 

• Rewritten expression: 113 × 9 + 17 − 519 ÷ 3.

 

• Apply BODMAS: 519 ÷ 3 = 173. 113 × 9 = 1017.

 

• 1017 + 17 − 173 = 1034 − 173 = 861.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option D.

 

SHORT TRICK

 

• First rewrite the ENTIRE expression with the correct (swapped) symbols before doing any arithmetic — solving symbol by symbol on the fly is a common source of error.

 

NOTE

 

• Once symbols are correctly swapped, apply standard BODMAS (division/multiplication before addition/subtraction) as usual.

question: A, B, C, R, S, T and U are sitting around a circular table, facing the centre of the table. R sits to the immediate left of U. B sits to the immediate left of C. C sits second to the left of T. A sits third to the left of U. Who sits third to the right of S?
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option C i.e. A.

 

GIVEN

 

• R is immediate left of U. B is immediate left of C. C is 2nd to the left of T. A is 3rd to the left of U.

 

SOLUTION
