• Use clockwise positions 0-6, 'left' = +1 step. Fix U = 0. Then R = U + 1 = 1, and A = U + 3 = 3.

 

• Let T = t. Since C is 2nd to the left of T: C = t + 2. Since B is immediate left of C: B = C + 1 = t + 3.

 

• The 7 positions {0,1,2,3,4,5,6} must all be used exactly once by U,R,A,T,C,B,S. With U=0,R=1,A=3 fixed, try T = 2: then C = 4, B = 5, and the only remaining position, 6, goes to S.

 

• Check all seven positions are distinct: 0(U),1(R),2(T),3(A),4(C),5(B),6(S) — ✓ all different, so this is the valid arrangement.

 

• 'Third to the right of S(6)' means moving 3 steps in the −1 (right) direction: 6 − 3 = 3, which is A.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option C.

 

SHORT TRICK

 

• Fix the person with the most 'anchor' clues (here U, referenced by 3 different conditions) at position 0 first — it resolves the rest of the puzzle fastest.

 

NOTE

 

• Since there are exactly 7 people and 7 seats, once a trial value (like T=2) fills every seat with no repeats or gaps, that confirms it is the unique valid arrangement.

question:

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option D.

question:
Based on the English alphabetical order, three of the following four letter-cluster pairs are alike in a certain way and thus form a group. Which letter-cluster pair DOES NOT belong to that group?

(Note: The odd one out is not based on the number of consonants/vowels or their position in the letter-cluster.)
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option B i.e. GK-EI.

 

GIVEN

 

• Four letter-cluster pairs: CG-AD, GK-EI, KO-IL, EI-CF.

 

SOLUTION

 

• Convert to positions (A=1...Z=26) and check the difference between each letter of the first cluster and the corresponding letter of the second cluster.

 

• CG(3,7)-AD(1,4): differences = 3−1=2, 7−4=3 → pattern (−2, −3).

 

• KO(11,15)-IL(9,12): differences = 11−9=2, 15−12=3 → pattern (−2, −3).

 

• EI(5,9)-CF(3,6): differences = 5−3=2, 9−6=3 → pattern (−2, −3).

 

• GK(7,11)-EI(5,9): differences = 7−5=2, 11−9=2 → pattern (−2, −2) — breaks the pattern.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option B.

 

SHORT TRICK

 

• Convert each letter pair to numbers and compute BOTH letter-differences — three pairs will show identical (first-letter diff, second-letter diff); the odd one out differs in the second value.

 

NOTE

 

• Don't stop checking after the first letter's difference matches — always verify the second letter's difference too, exactly as in Q51 of this same paper.

question:
A group of numbers/symbols is coded using letter codes as per the codes given below and the conditions that follow. The correct combination of codes following the conditions is your answer.

Note: If none of the conditions apply, then the codes for the respective number/symbol are to be followed directly as given in the table.

 

Numbers/symbols: % 8 2 $ 6 3 ÷ 7 @ 9 * 5 # 4

Codes: S D R P K H L G B U C N W Q

 

Conditions:

(i) If both the second and third elements are perfect squares, the codes for these two (the second and third elements) are to be interchanged.

(ii) If the first element and the third element are even numbers, these two (the first and third elements) are to be coded as &.

(iii) If both the second and third elements are multiples of 3, the third element is to be coded as the code for the second element.

What will be the code for the following group?

$ 9 6 @ 7
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option D i.e. P U U B G.

 

GIVEN

 

• Group to code: $ 9 6 @ 7. Base codes from the table: $ = P, 9 = U, 6 = K, @ = B, 7 = G.

 

SOLUTION

 

• Check condition (i): are the 2nd (9) and 3rd (6) elements both perfect squares? 9 is a perfect square (3²) but 6 is not — condition doesn't apply.

 

• Check condition (ii): are the 1st ($) and 3rd (6) elements both even numbers? $ is a symbol, not a number at all — condition doesn't apply.

 

• Check condition (iii): are the 2nd (9) and 3rd (6) elements both multiples of 3? 9 = 3×3 ✓ and 6 = 3×2 ✓ — condition applies: the 3rd element (6) is now coded as the code for the 2nd element (9), i.e. 6 is coded as U instead of K.

 

• Final codes: $ = P, 9 = U, 6 = U (overridden), @ = B, 7 = G.

 

• So the group $ 9 6 @ 7 is coded as P U U B G.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option D.

 

SHORT TRICK

 

• Check the conditions strictly in order and verify EACH part of a condition (e.g. 'both are perfect squares') before applying it — a condition never applies if even one part fails.

 

NOTE

 

• A symbol (like $, @, ÷) can never be classified as 'odd', 'even', a 'perfect square' or a 'multiple of 3' — only the actual numbers in the group can trigger conditions (i), (ii) or (iii).

question: Mayank starts from Point A and drives 9 km towards the East. He then takes a left turn, drives 6 km, turns left and drives 17 km. He then takes a left turn and drives 15 km. He takes a final left turn, drives 8 km and stops at Point P. How far (shortest distance) and towards which direction should he drive in order to reach Point A again? (All turns are 90 degrees turns only unless specified.)
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option A i.e. 9 km to the North.

 

GIVEN

 

• Start at A, facing East; moves: 9 km East → left → 6 km → left → 17 km → left → 15 km → left → 8 km, stopping at P.

 

SOLUTION

 

• Take A = (0,0), facing East. Move 9 km East: (9, 0).

 

• Left turn from East → North. Move 6 km North: (9, 6).

 

• Left turn from North → West. Move 17 km West: (9−17, 6) = (−8, 6).

 

• Left turn from West → South. Move 15 km South: (−8, 6−15) = (−8, −9).

 

• Left turn from South → East. Move 8 km East: (−8+8, −9) = (0, −9). This is point P.

 

• Distance from P(0,−9) to A(0,0) = 9 km. Since A is above P (0 > −9), A lies due North of P.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option A.

 

SHORT TRICK

 

• Plot the path on an X-Y grid with East = +x and North = +y; each 'left turn' rotates the facing direction 90° anticlockwise (E→N→W→S→E) — track only the final coordinates, not the whole path.

 

NOTE

 

• The direction FROM P TO A (the answer) is the opposite of the direction from A to P — always double-check which direction the question is asking for.

question:
In the following triads, each group of letters is related to the subsequent one following a certain logic. Select from the given options, the one which follows the same logic.

 

FOUR - ORUF - RUOF

TENS - ESNT - SNET
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option A i.e. PLUG - LGUP - GULP.

 

GIVEN

 

• FOUR → ORUF → RUOF, and TENS → ESNT → SNET both follow the same hidden logic.

 

SOLUTION

 

• Step 1 (word1 → word2): rearrange positions as [letter2, letter4, letter3, letter1]. FOUR(F,O,U,R) → (O,R,U,F) = ORUF ✓. TENS(T,E,N,S) → (E,S,N,T) = ESNT ✓.

 

• Step 2 (word2 → word3): rearrange as [letter2, letter3, letter1, letter4]. ORUF(O,R,U,F) → (R,U,O,F) = RUOF ✓. ESNT(E,S,N,T) → (S,N,E,T) = SNET ✓.

 

• Apply to PLUG(P,L,U,G): Step 1 → [L,G,U,P] = LGUP (matches given word2 form).

 

• Apply Step 2 to LGUP(L,G,U,P): → [G,U,L,P] = GULP (matches given word3 form).

 

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option A.

 

SHORT TRICK

 

• Track exact letter POSITIONS (1st, 2nd, 3rd, 4th) moving from word1→word2, then word2→word3, and apply the identical positional rule to each option — don't just look for a superficial resemblance.

 

NOTE

 

• Testing only the first transformation against each option quickly eliminates 3 of the 4 choices before checking the second transformation in detail.

question:
In the following triads, each group of letters is related to the subsequent one following a certain logic. Select from the given options, the one which follows the same logic.

 

BLUE - LBUE - ELBU

TWIN - WTIN - NWTI
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option A i.e. FOUR - OFUR - ROFU.

 

GIVEN

 

• BLUE → LBUE → ELBU, and TWIN → WTIN → NWTI both follow the same hidden logic.

 

SOLUTION

 

• Step 1 (word1 → word2): swap the 1st and 2nd letters, keep the 3rd and 4th unchanged. BLUE(B,L,U,E) → (L,B,U,E) = LBUE ✓. TWIN(T,W,I,N) → (W,T,I,N) = WTIN ✓.

 

• Step 2 (word2 → word3): rotate the whole word right by one place (last letter moves to the front). LBUE(L,B,U,E) → (E,L,B,U) = ELBU ✓. WTIN(W,T,I,N) → (N,W,T,I) = NWTI ✓.

 

• Apply to FOUR(F,O,U,R): Step 1 (swap 1st & 2nd) → (O,F,U,R) = OFUR (matches given word2 form).

 

• Apply Step 2 to OFUR(O,F,U,R): rotate right by one → (R,O,F,U) = ROFU (matches given word3 form).

 

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option A.

 

SHORT TRICK

 

• Recognise 'swap first two letters' and 'rotate whole word right by one' as two of the most common triad transformations tested — memorising these speeds up pattern recognition considerably.

 

NOTE

 

• A right rotation moves the LAST letter to the FRONT of the word (not the first letter to the back, which would be a left rotation) — the two are easy to confuse.

question:
Refer to the following number, symbol series and answer the question. Counting to be done from left to right only. All numbers are single-digit numbers.

 

(Left) % € € % 6 £ 3 & 1 £ 4 5 7 2 2 & & 9 & 8 8 * (Right)

 

How many such symbols are there each of which is immediately preceded by a number and also immediately followed by a number?
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option B i.e. 4.

 

GIVEN

 

• Series: % € € % 6 £ 3 & 1 £ 4 5 7 2 2 & & 9 & 8 8 * (22 terms; %, €, £, &, * are symbols; 6,3,1,4,5,7,2,2,9,8,8 are numbers).

 

SOLUTION

 

• Scan for a symbol with a number immediately before AND immediately after it.

 

• The £ after 6: preceded by 6 (number) ✓, followed by 3 (number) ✓ — counts.

 

• The & after 3: preceded by 3 (number) ✓, followed by 1 (number) ✓ — counts.

 

• The £ after 1: preceded by 1 (number) ✓, followed by 4 (number) ✓ — counts.

 

• The & after 9: preceded by 9 (number) ✓, followed by 8 (number) ✓ — counts.

 

• All other symbols (the two €'s at the start, the % at the start, and the run of &'s together, and the final *) fail because a symbol (not a number) sits on at least one side. Total = 4.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option B.

 

SHORT TRICK

 

• Mark all the symbol positions first, then check only their immediate left and right neighbour for 'number' status — far quicker than repeatedly scanning the whole series.

 

NOTE

 

• Consecutive symbols (like & & appearing together) automatically disqualify each other from this condition, since at least one neighbour is also a symbol.

question:
Read the given statements and conclusions carefully. Assuming that the information given in the statements is true, even if it appears to be at variance with commonly known facts, decide which of the given conclusions logically follow(s) from the statements.

 

Statements:

Some cars are vehicles.

All vehicles are machines.

 

Conclusions

(I): Some machines are cars.

(II): No cars are machines.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option D i.e. Only conclusion (I) follows.

 

GIVEN

 

• Statement 1: Some cars are vehicles (Car ∩ Vehicle ≠ ∅). Statement 2: All vehicles are machines (Vehicle ⊂ Machine).

 

SOLUTION

 

• Since some cars are vehicles, and ALL vehicles are machines, those particular 'car-vehicles' must also be machines.

 

• This directly gives: Some cars are machines, which is the same as saying Some machines are cars — so Conclusion I follows.

 

• Conclusion II ('No cars are machines') directly contradicts what was just proven in Conclusion I, so it cannot follow.

 

• Since Conclusion I follows and Conclusion II does not, the answer is 'Only conclusion (I) follows'.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option D.

 

SHORT TRICK

 

• Draw a simple Venn diagram: a small Car circle overlapping a Vehicle circle, with the Vehicle circle entirely inside the Machine circle — the overlap region between Car and Vehicle automatically falls inside Machine too, proving 'Some cars are machines'.

 

NOTE

 

• 'Some A are B' + 'All B are C' always validly gives 'Some A are C' (and its converse 'Some C are A') — a standard syllogism pattern worth memorising.

question:
Select the set in which the numbers are related in the same way as are the numbers of the following sets.

(NOTE: Operations should be performed on the whole numbers, without breaking down the numbers into their constituent digits. E.g. 13 – Operations on 13 such as adding/subtracting/multiplying to 13 can be performed. Breaking down 13 into 1 and 3 and then performing mathematical operations on 1 and 3 is not allowed.)

 

(18, 15.7, 19.2)

(24, 21.7, 25.2)
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option D i.e. (31, 28.7, 32.2).

 

GIVEN

 

• Reference sets: (18, 15.7, 19.2) and (24, 21.7, 25.2). Note: the printed options contain a transcription artifact where the middle number's leading digits appear replaced by the option's own letter (e.g. 'D).7' in place of the actual digits before the decimal) — this is reproduced here exactly as it appears in the source, but the intended numeric values are decoded below.

 

SOLUTION

 

• In each reference set, check the relation of the 1st number to the 2nd and 3rd: 18 − 2.3 = 15.7 ✓, and 18 + 1.2 = 19.2 ✓.

 

• Verify with the second set: 24 − 2.3 = 21.7 ✓, and 24 + 1.2 = 25.2 ✓. So the rule is: (2nd number) = (1st number) − 2.3, and (3rd number) = (1st number) + 1.2.

 

• Testing Option D's first number, 31: 31 − 2.3 = 28.7, and 31 + 1.2 = 32.2, which exactly matches the printed third value '32.2' and decodes the garbled middle term as 28.7.

 

• None of the other options' first numbers (37, 28, 9) produce values matching their own printed third term under this rule.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option D.

 

SHORT TRICK

 

• Once you find a consistent additive rule from the two clean reference sets (here, −2.3 and +1.2 from the first number), simply apply it to each option's first number and check which one is internally consistent.

 

NOTE

 

• The garbled formatting in the options (e.g. 'D).7') is preserved exactly as printed in the source paper; working from the two fully-legible reference sets is the reliable way to find the true numerical pattern.

question: Seven boxes M, N, O, P, Q, R and S are kept one over the other but not necessarily in the same order. Only two boxes are kept below S. Only one box is kept above Q. Only one box is kept between Q and P. R is kept immediately above N. O is kept at some place below M. How many boxes are kept between M and R?
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option B i.e. Four.

 

GIVEN

 

• 7 boxes stacked, positions 1 (bottom) to 7 (top). Only 2 below S; only 1 above Q; only 1 between Q and P; R immediately above N; O somewhere below M.

 

SOLUTION

 

• 'Only two boxes below S' ⇒ S is at position 3. 'Only one box above Q' ⇒ Q is at position 6.

 

• 'Only one box between Q and P' ⇒ P is 2 away from Q(6): P = 4 or 8(invalid), so P = 4.

 

• Remaining positions {1, 2, 5, 7} are for M, N, O, R. Since R is immediately above N (R = N + 1), and only (1,2) is a consecutive pair among {1,2,5,7}, we get N = 1, R = 2.

 

• Remaining positions {5, 7} go to O and M, with O below M: so O = 5, M = 7.

 

• Final stack (bottom→top): N(1), R(2), S(3), P(4), O(5), Q(6), M(7).

 

• Boxes between M(7) and R(2): positions 3, 4, 5, 6 (i.e. S, P, O, Q) — that's Four boxes.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option B.

 

SHORT TRICK

 

• Convert 'only N boxes below/above X' clues directly into fixed position numbers first (they pin down exact positions immediately) before tackling relative clues like 'immediately above'.

 

NOTE

 

• Once several positions are fixed, look for the ONLY possible consecutive pair among the remaining open slots to resolve 'immediately above/below' clues without guesswork.

question:
Read the given statements and conclusions carefully. Assuming that the information given in the statements is true, even if it appears to be at variance with commonly known facts, decide which of the given conclusions logically follow(s) from the statements.

 

Statements:

All pathways are roads.

No pathway is a garden.

 

Conclusions:

(I): Some gardens are roads.

(II): All roads are gardens.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option C i.e. Neither conclusion (I) nor (II) follows.

 

GIVEN

 

• Statement 1: All pathways are roads (Pathway ⊂ Road). Statement 2: No pathway is a garden (Pathway ∩ Garden = ∅).

 

SOLUTION

 

• Roads may include pathways (all of which are non-gardens) as well as many other, unrelated roads about which nothing is stated — so we cannot conclude anything definite about whether 'some' or 'all' roads are gardens.

 

• Conclusion I ('Some gardens are roads') would require positive evidence linking gardens to roads, but the statements only tell us pathways are NOT gardens — this gives no basis to conclude any garden IS a road. Does not follow.

 

• Conclusion II ('All roads are gardens') is actually contradicted by the statements — since pathways ARE roads but are explicitly NOT gardens, it is false that ALL roads are gardens. Does not follow.

 

• Hence neither conclusion follows.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option C.

 

SHORT TRICK

 

• A statement of the form 'No A is B' combined with 'All A are C' tells you only that some C's (the A's) are not B — it never supports a positive 'Some B are C' or a universal 'All C are B' conclusion.

 

NOTE

 

• Draw the Venn diagram: Pathway circle fully inside Road circle, with Pathway circle NOT overlapping Garden circle at all — Garden's relationship to the rest of Road remains completely undefined, so no conclusion about it can be drawn.

question: Mr. Zzz starts from Point A and drives 8 km towards east. He then takes a right turn, drives 11 km, turns right and drives 17 km. He then takes a right turn and drives 21 km. He takes a final right turn, drives 9 km and stops at Point P. How far (shortest distance) and towards which direction should he drive in order to reach Point A again? (All turns are 90-degree turns only, unless specified.)
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option B i.e. 10 km to the south.

 

GIVEN

 

• Start at A, facing East; moves: 8 km East → right → 11 km → right → 17 km → right → 21 km → right → 9 km, stopping at P.

 

SOLUTION

• Right turn from East → South. Move 11 km South: (8, −11).

• Right turn from North → East. Move 9 km East: (−9+9, 10) = (0, 10). This is point P.

 

• Distance from P(0,10) to A(0,0) = 10 km. Since A is below P (0 < 10), A lies due South of P.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option B.

 

SHORT TRICK

 

• On a coordinate grid (East = +x, North = +y), each right turn rotates the facing direction 90° clockwise (E→S→W→N→E) — track only the running (x,y) position, not the full path shape.

 

NOTE

 

• Always find the direction FROM the final point P TO the starting point A, which is the reverse of A's direction relative to P.

solution_text:

question: In which of the following cities was the inauguration of the Recognition of Prior Learning – Certification in Indian Sign Language Interpretation (RPL–CISLI) programme held in August 2025?

question: According to the India BioEconomy Report 2025, how much is India's BioEconomy valued at in 2024?

question: Which among the following civic suggestions did Karnataka's Deputy Chief Minister give in September 2025 to improve governance quality in Bengaluru?

• The suggestion emphasises citizen accountability and transparency — timely payment of property/civic taxes, honest declaration of assets, and avoidance of concealment — as a foundation for better urban governance.

• Karnataka's Chief Minister at this time was Siddaramaiah, with D.K. Shivakumar serving as Deputy Chief Minister and Karnataka Pradesh Congress Committee (KPCC) president.

 

NOTE

question: World Environment Day was observed on 5 June 2025 with a special focus to end which of the following?

question: On 20th May, 2025, the Supreme Court (SC) reinstated the requirement of how many years of legal practice for law graduates to apply for civil judge (junior division) posts, reversing its 2002 decision?
solution_text:
The correct answer is 3 years.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• On 20 May 2025, the Supreme Court of India ruled that candidates must have at least 3 years of practice as an advocate to be eligible to apply for the post of Civil Judge (Junior Division), reversing its own 2002 judgment (in the All India Judges' Association case) which had removed this requirement. (सिविल जज पात्रता — 3 वर्ष विधि अभ्यास)

 

• The Court held that fresh law graduates lacked adequate courtroom exposure and practical experience to handle judicial responsibilities effectively, hence the reinstated experience requirement.

 

• The ruling also required candidates to produce certificates from an advocate (with 10 years' standing) and a judicial officer to prove their years of actual practice.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option C.

 

Additional Information

 

• The 2002 judgment (All India Judges' Association vs Union of India) had earlier scrapped the minimum practice requirement, allowing fresh law graduates to appear directly for judicial service exams.

 

• The recruitment of judges to the subordinate judiciary is conducted through State Judicial Services Examinations, held separately by each state's High Court/Public Service Commission.

 

NOTE

 

• 2 years, 4 years, 5 years (Options A, B, D): Do not match the specific 3-year practice requirement reinstated by the Supreme Court in this May 2025 ruling.

question: In June 2025, the Department of Financial Services (DFS), Ministry of Finance, convened a high-level meeting co-chaired by M Nagaraju, Secretary, Department of Financial Services and T Rabi Sankar, Deputy Governor, RBI at New Delhi, on scaling up ULI. What is the full form of ULI?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Unified Lending Interface.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• ULI stands for Unified Lending Interface, a digital public infrastructure initiative by the Reserve Bank of India (RBI) to enable frictionless, consent-based digital credit delivery by aggregating financial and non-financial data from multiple sources. (यूनिफाइड लेंडिंग इंटरफेस — RBI की डिजिटल ऋण पहल)

 

• ULI works on principles similar to the Unified Payments Interface (UPI) — enabling seamless, standardised access for lenders to borrower data (land records, credit history, etc.) with consent, speeding up loan approvals especially for farmers, MSMEs and small borrowers.

 

• The June 2025 meeting, co-chaired by M. Nagaraju (Secretary, DFS) and T. Rabi Sankar (Deputy Governor, RBI), reviewed the pace of ULI adoption and onboarding of banks/NBFCs and data providers onto the platform.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option A.

 

Additional Information

 

• ULI was first announced/piloted around 2023-24 and is envisioned to do for lending what UPI did for payments in India.

 

• Key Digital Public Infrastructure (DPI) components of India's 'India Stack' include Aadhaar, UPI, DigiLocker and now ULI.

 

NOTE

 

• Universal Loan Identifier (Option B), Unique Lending Index (Option C) and Urban Lending Interface (Option D): Plausible-sounding but incorrect expansions of ULI — the officially used term is 'Unified Lending Interface'.

question: Which country was ranked highest for gender equality in the Global Gender Gap Report, 2025, released by the World Economic Forum in May 2025?

Therefore, the correct answer is Option C.

 

Additional Information

question: India is drafting its first comprehensive framework, National Adaptation Plan (NAP), to be submitted to the United Nations Framework Convention on Climate Change (UNFCCC) by September 2025 in compliance with the _____.
solution_text:
The correct answer is Paris Agreement.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• India's National Adaptation Plan (NAP), its first comprehensive climate-adaptation framework, is being drafted in compliance with the Paris Agreement, which requires member countries to engage in national adaptation planning processes. (राष्ट्रीय अनुकूलन योजना — पेरिस समझौता)

 

• The Paris Agreement (2015), adopted at COP21 under the UNFCCC, aims to limit global warming to well below 2°C, preferably to 1.5°C, above pre-industrial levels, and obligates countries to submit both mitigation (NDCs) and adaptation plans.

 

• The NAP focuses on strengthening India's resilience to climate impacts such as heatwaves, floods, droughts and sea-level rise, across sectors like agriculture, water resources, health and infrastructure.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option D.

 

Additional Information

 

• India ratified the Paris Agreement in October 2016, and its climate commitments are captured through its Nationally Determined Contributions (NDCs).

 

• India has also committed to achieving net-zero emissions by 2070, announced by PM Modi at COP26 in Glasgow (2021).

 

NOTE

 

• Kyoto Protocol (Option A): The earlier (1997) climate treaty under UNFCCC that set binding emission-reduction targets mainly for developed countries; superseded in scope by the Paris Agreement.

 

• Cartagena Protocol (Option B): Relates to biosafety and the transboundary movement of living modified organisms, under the Convention on Biological Diversity — unrelated to NAP.

 

• Montreal Convention (Option C): Actually the 'Montreal Protocol' relates to phasing out ozone-depleting substances, not climate adaptation planning under UNFCCC.

question: Who among the following was appointed as Executive Director of the Reserve Bank of India in March 2025 to look after the Department of Statistics and Information Management and Financial Stability Department?
